tours.ticketSummary: Mail becomes work, work gets handed over, an outside process does its part, and the decision leaves as a signed fact. About five minutes.
tours.ticketStep1: You are looking at a whole product running from one file, with a simulated world around it. The dark panel on the right is the Simulator: the control room for that world, not part of the product. Its People tab lists everyone who lives here, so press Next to become Dana Okoye, who runs the frontline support desk.
tours.ticketStep2: Dana's desk does not open empty. Five tickets, two of them unclaimed, and NW-1028 has been waiting four days. A demo should start inside a situation rather than build one from nothing.
tours.ticketStep3: A support desk is really a mailbox that becomes work, and the Simulator can post mail into the app. This one comes from Dana's own address on purpose: a stranger's mail is filed and ignored, because writing in by email grants exactly what the screen grants. Read it, then press Next to send it.
tours.ticketStep4: The intake log says handled, and the desk has a new ticket: NW-1042, open, unassigned, its body the text of the email. Nobody typed it into the product.
tours.ticketStep5: Work gets handed to a person. The picker beside NW-1042 holds this team's members. Press Next to give it to Sam Rivera.
tours.ticketStep6: Sam is the one told about it, not the team's admins, and here is the copy in his inbox. Hand a ticket to yourself and nobody is told at all, which is the whole point of having a rule about who hears.
tours.ticketStep7: Some work is slow, so the desk hands it off and gets on with something else. The simulated world normally finishes that background work instantly, so press Next to hold the jobs and watch who picks the next one up.
tours.ticketStep8: Ticket NW-1039 arrived with a customer's diagnostic bundle, a log too big to read by hand. Only bundles offer Analyze, because only bundles are worth an outside analyzer's time. Press Next to send it over.
tours.ticketStep9: Nobody clicked anything. The bundle analyzer is a separate simulated process with its own credentials, asking for work of its own accord: its log on the right is every call it actually made, and the job on the left is finished.
tours.ticketStep10: The escalation on NW-1039 belongs to two teams: the desk that raised it, and the team that has to answer. Dana runs both, so switching teams puts the decision in front of her. A plain member of that team would see the same row with no buttons on it.
tours.ticketStep11: Before deciding, say where the decision should go. This registers a webhook on the answering team: an address to post to, and the one event worth hearing about. Press Next to save it.
tours.ticketStep12: Now the decision itself. Press Next to accept the escalation, and watch what leaves the building when she does.
tours.ticketStep13: The decision is queued for the endpoint that asked to hear about it. Nothing has been sent yet, which is the truth about outbound work: it waits its turn. Press Next to let the world make the attempt.
tours.ticketStep14: Delivered, and signed: the envelope that went over the wire, the signature a receiver checks it against, the attempt count. Make this endpoint fail from here and you can watch the retries back off and give up.
tours.ticketStep15: That is the loop. Mail becomes work, work gets handed over, an outside process does its part, and the decision leaves as a fact other systems can trust. Everything you just watched is yours to click now, and the jobs are still held: the knob is in Snapshots.
tours.inviteTitle: Joining the desk, from a preset
tours.inviteSummary: Starts mid-shift from the mid-demo preset and walks a pending invite until the newcomer is a member. About two minutes.
tours.inviteStep1: This tour did not start from the seed. It loaded the mid-demo preset: Dana's desk partway through a shift, with two emails already turned into tickets. A preset is a script the world replays, so it loads the same way here and on a server.
tours.inviteStep2: The same preset invited a new teammate, Jordan, who has not joined yet — the People tab lists them as invited. Press Next to sit at Jordan's desk.
tours.inviteStep3: Jordan has no account, so the product shows the signed-out welcome page while the panel follows them. Their inbox already holds the invite, unread.
tours.inviteStep4: The invite carries a link to the accept page. Press Next to follow it.
tours.inviteStep5: The accept page names the team Jordan is joining. A name is all it takes — press Next to join the desk.
tours.inviteStep6: Accepting signed Jordan straight in, as a member of the Frontline Desk.
tours.inviteStep7: Back in the People tab, Jordan is an active person now, no longer an invite.
tours.inviteStep8: Every preset lives in the Snapshots tab. Load one before a demo and you start inside the story, on whichever host you happen to be running.
